springs.title: The Regenerative Practitioner, Lisbon cohort
springs.where: Online, with a three-day intensive at Gandum Village, near Lisbon
springs.text: Learn regenerative development by working with a real project, alongside practitioners from many places and fields. Open to people anywhere, with a special welcome for Europe and Portugal. Co-taught by Nuno da Silva and Constança Belchior of Lucida. Sliding-scale discounts and scholarships are offered.
springs.costNote: Paid, with sliding scale and scholarships

springs.title: BioFi Deep Dive: building farmer-owned regenerative supply systems
springs.when: Monday 14 December 2026, 11:30am to 1pm Eastern (8:30 to 10am Pacific)
springs.text: The last BioFi Deep Dive of 2026, with Luke Smith, co-founder of Origins Co-op. Origins is building farmer-owned market infrastructure with around 500 smallholder farmers in southern Thailand who are turning rubber plantations into diverse agroforests. A rich look at how whole watersheds could move to regenerative farming together.
springs.found: Shared by Joe, from the BioFi Project newsletter

springs.title: Sense the Shift: Business and Stewardship, with Darshita Gillies
springs.when: Thursday 3 December 2026, 6:30pm GMT (10:30am Pacific), 75 to 90 minutes
springs.text: A live, dialogue-led conversation about what a business holds in trust, and how honestly it can account for its effects on people and the planet. Darshita Gillies founded Maanch, a B Corp building stewardship tools for investors. A gentle first step on the Canal toward relational business.
springs.costNote: Join free, or give what you can
springs.found: Shared by Joe, who met ESSENSE through Beena Sharma

springs.title: Sense the Shift: Business and Imagination, with Phoebe Tickell
springs.when: Thursday 17 December 2026, 6:30pm GMT (10:30am Pacific), about 90 minutes
springs.text: How might business help shape the future rather than only react to it? A live conversation on growing the imagination to question inherited systems and design more regenerative, participatory organisations, with Phoebe Tickell, founder of Moral Imaginations.
springs.costNote: £35 for a one-talk pass, as listed on their page
springs.found: Shared by Joe, who met ESSENSE through Beena Sharma

springs.host: The Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation
springs.title: The Power of Invertebrates: Connecting People and Landscapes for a Better World
springs.where: Online, on Zoom, with captions; recorded for later
springs.text: A year-end celebration with Scott Black, director of the Xerces Society, on how insects and other invertebrates connect species, people, landscapes, food and the health of the planet, and how caring for bees, butterflies, fireflies and freshwater mussels keeps food webs whole and brings communities together. A gentle way to meet the small Beings who hold so much together.
springs.found: Shared by Joe, a member of the Xerces Society community
